diagnostic_evidence.quote: The computational complexity includes $O(\tau\cdot\texttt{nnz(S)}d)$ flops for computing the sketched Newton direction and $O(d^2)$~flops for updating $\hat{\Xi}_t$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a sparse block sketch S consisting of q coordinate columns, nnz(S)=q, but B_tS is generally dense. Evaluating the stated recursion includes forming its q-by-q Gram matrix and computing a pseudoinverse, with conventional costs O(dq^2+q^3). These are not bounded by O(dq) when q grows; q≪d does not make q constant. No alternative computation eliminating these costs is supplied.

failure_location.quote: Specifically,~the~time~complexity can be reduced to $O(\texttt{nnz(S)}d)$, where $S\in\mR^{d\times q}$ is the sketching matrix with $q\ll d$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the Gram-matrix and pseudoinverse costs, or explicitly restrict the cheaper bound to vector or fixed-width sketches. The coordinate-vector O(d^2) inference example can remain.
issues.overall_effect: The stated direction-computation and general inference complexity bounds are unsupported for growing sparse multi-column sketches.
issues.title: The sketching complexity bound omits multi-column Gram-matrix costs
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a substantive qualification of the claimed complexity, but preserves the principal vector-sketch implementation and all statistical rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout the paper, we let $\mF_t = \sigma(\{\xi_i\}_{i=0}^t)$, for any $t\geq 0$, be the filtration~of~$\sigma$-algebras generated by the sample sequence $\xi_0, \xi_1,\xi_2\ldots$.

issues.failure_explanation: The iterate x_t depends on previous sketches and potentially additional stepsize randomness, neither of which belongs to the defined filtration. Consequently x_t, B_t, and ∇F_t need not be F_{t-1}-measurable. Even for a quadratic objective with independent data, the conditional mean is E[∇F(x_t) | F_{t-1}], not generally ∇F(x_t). The subsequent martingale and conditional-expectation calculations repeatedly assume the missing measurability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the full algorithmic history, including sketches and auxiliary stepsize randomness, and formulate adaptedness and the conditional assumptions relative to that history.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional unbiasedness assertions and the adaptedness required by the convergence, moment, and covariance proofs are not justified with the stated filtration.
issues.title: The filtration omits randomness needed for adaptedness
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local correction to the probability setup that preserves the intended online method, parameter regimes, and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is important to note that the sketching distribution used in our experiments does~not introduce bias when $\Sigma_a = I$.
When $\tilde{\Xi}_t$ is a consistent estimator (i.e., when $\Sigma_a = I$ or $\tau = \infty$), $\hat{\Xi}_t$ performs competitively compared to $\tilde{\Xi}_t$.

issues.failure_explanation: A nonvanishing upper-bound term O((1−γ_S)^τ) does not establish a nonzero limiting bias. Indeed, the paper itself acknowledges finite-τ consistency in the identity-design case. Algebraically, with B*=I, isotropic gradient noise, coordinate sketches, and β<1, the Lyapunov equation gives Xi*=Omega*/2 for every finite τ, exactly the plug-in target.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\tilde{\Xi}_t$ is a biased estimator~of $\Xi^\star$, leading to invalid confidence coverage even as $t\rightarrow\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that ignoring sketching can produce asymptotic bias, identify the possibility of zero-bias exceptions, and do not infer inconsistency from an upper bound alone.
issues.overall_effect: The universal claims that only exact Newton solves permit plug-in consistency, and that finite sketching necessarily causes invalid limiting coverage, are false.
issues.title: Finite sketching does not necessarily make the plug-in estimator inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A substantive universal comparison must be weakened, although the proposed estimator and the general concern about plug-in bias remain intact.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions impose only upper noise-moment bounds and allow Xi* to be singular or zero. For deterministic f(x)=||x||^2/2 initialized at x*=0, all iterates and covariance estimates are zero: the region's inverse is undefined and the scalar interval covers with probability one, not 1−q. Independently of noise degeneracy, the stated inclusion of w=0 always gives coverage one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require Xi* to be positive definite for the full-dimensional region and require w^T Xi* w>0 for a directional interval. Specify a harmless convention on finite-sample singular-estimator events.
issues.overall_effect: The chi-square region and exact nominal directional coverage do not follow from the possibly degenerate Gaussian limit allowed by the hypotheses.
issues.title: Confidence guarantees omit nondegeneracy conditions
issues.why_classification: Standard local nondegeneracy conditions repair studentization without changing the estimator, its convergence rates, or the nondegenerate inference procedure.

issues.failure_explanation: The recursion requires an existing inverse, but the prescribed covariance starts at zero and has rank at most t−1. In particular, hatXi_1=0 and hatXi_t is necessarily singular for t≤d. The formula is also undefined at t=0. Positive definiteness of the limiting covariance would not supply the missing starting inverse.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a complete inverse-startup procedure, or explicitly use a ridge-seeded covariance hatXi_t+(λ/t)I for t≥1, initialize its inverse at t=1, and apply the Appendix Woodbury update to that modified matrix. The O(1/t) ridge leaves the asymptotic statistical rates unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised fully online, factorization-free confidence-region implementation is not an executable procedure from the supplied initialization.
issues.title: The online inverse recursion has no valid initialization
issues.why_classification: A complete resolution requires an additional initialization construction or a modified inverse estimator; merely adding population nondegeneracy does not repair the algorithm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the convergence rate of the batch-means estimators is $O(1/\sqrt[4]{t\beta_t})$
Under the conditions in Lemma \ref{sec4:lem1}, except for strengthening $\chi>\beta$ to $\chi>1.5\beta$,

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's rate includes χ_t/β_t^{1.5}, whose decay can be arbitrarily slow under χ>1.5β. For example, β=0.6 and χ=0.91 give an asserted bound dominated by t^{-0.01}, whereas the quoted batch-means bound is t^{-0.1}. Thus the theorem does not establish the unqualified faster-convergence comparison throughout its allowed adaptive-stepsize regime.

failure_location.quote: which is slower than that of $\hat{\Xi}_t$~in~\mbox{Theorem}~\ref{sec4:thm1}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the comparison by a sufficiently fast decay of the adaptation window, such as χ≥2β, or explicitly compare both terms of the proved bound.
issues.overall_effect: The general comparative-rate claim, repeated in the conclusion, exceeds the rate actually proved.
issues.title: The faster-than-batch-means comparison ignores the adaptivity term
issues.why_classification: The claimed advantage needs a substantive parameter-regime qualification, while the underlying consistency theorem remains unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem concerns the specified Hessian average, and its proof crucially makes B_t−B* vanish at a quantitative rate. A non-Hessian limiting conditioner changes the leading drift and limiting covariance, not merely a remainder. For example, in one dimension with Hessian h, constant conditioner b, and gradient-noise variance v, the β<1 covariance is v/(2bh), whereas the Newton covariance used here is v/(2h^2). These differ when b≠h.

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does~not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to~the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the applicability claim to the Hessian-average construction actually analyzed. Retaining the non-Hessian extension requires a separate theorem with the appropriate drift, Lyapunov covariance, and control of preconditioner errors.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed consistency guarantee for general conditioned SGD, including the named non-Newton methods, is not a consequence of the stated theorem or its proof.
issues.title: Direct applicability to non-Hessian conditioned SGD is not established
issues.why_classification: The source-supported restriction removes the entire advertised non-Hessian-conditioning extension; no comparable extension theorem is established in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For this model, we use the~squared~loss~defined as $f(\bx; \xi) = \frac{1}{2}(\xi_{b}-\bxi_{a}^T\bx)^2$.
\State\textbf{Input:} initial iterate $\bx_0$, positive sequences $\{\beta_t, \chi_t\}$, an integer $\tau>0$, $B_0 = I$;

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated linear regression loss, H_0=a_0a_0^T has rank one. The averaging rule overwrites the identity seed, giving B_1=H_0 and rank(B_t)≤t for t<d. With independent Gaussian features, the next gradient is almost surely outside range(B_1), so the exact Newton system has no solution, and the plug-in inverse is undefined. Logistic regression has the same rank-one sample-Hessian startup problem.

failure_location.quote: For~both plug-in estimator $\tilde{\Xi}_t$ and our sample covariance estimator $\hat{\Xi}_t$, we implement sketched Newton~methods with varying sketching steps $\tau\in\{10,20,40,\infty\}$. When $\tau=\infty$, the scheme reduces to~the~\mbox{standard} Newton method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify a positive-definite Hessian initialization that is retained in the average, or collect a full-rank pilot sample before inversion, and make the experimental comparisons correspond to that modified procedure.
issues.overall_effect: The exact-Newton and plug-in regression experiments cannot be executed as specified; an unstated regularization or warm start is necessary.
issues.title: The regression implementation encounters singular Hessian averages immediately
issues.why_classification: A contained but substantive change to the experimental algorithm is needed; the supplied identity initialization does not itself prevent the failure.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated asymptotic equivalence does not control consecutive ratios to accuracy o(1/i). For example, varphi_i=c(i+1)^{-varphi}(1+(-1)^i/log(i+2)) satisfies the hypothesis, but its oscillations make the displayed scaled ratio fail to converge, even when phi_i is an exact negative power. The application of Lemma aux:lem1 through this claimed limit is therefore unjustified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use auxiliary weights formed from the exact power c(i+1)^{-varphi}, which have the required ratio limit, and control the asymptotically equivalent weight differences through Lemma aux:lem1's vanishing-error assertion.
issues.overall_effect: The proof is incomplete for the general perturbations permitted by the preparation lemma. The paper's actual centered power-law stepsizes do have the additional ratio regularity.
issues.title: An asymptotic equivalent is incorrectly used to infer a consecutive-ratio limit
issues.why_classification: A short local asymptotic-comparison argument preserves the lemma's bounds and all applications without changing a rate or construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $t\geq 0$, we assume the sketching matrix $S_{t,j}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}S$ satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: Being iid among sketches does not imply independence from the current data sample. A concrete permitted coupling has d=1, B_t=1, iid Bernoulli bits Z_{t,j} contained in ξ_t, S_{t,j}=Z_{t,j}, M_t the indicator that all bits vanish, p=2^{-τ}, and f(x;ξ_t)=x^2/2+(M_t−p)x. The stated marginal, Hessian, and moment conditions hold, but the sketched direction is −(1−M_t)(x_t−p), whose conditional mean is −(1−p)(x_t−p), not −(1−p)x_t. With admissible deterministic stepsizes it converges to p rather than x*=0.

failure_location.quote: By the independence between sketching and sampling and the unbiasedness of $\barg_t$ in Assumption \ref{ass:2}, we complete the proof of (b).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly require fresh sketch blocks to be independent of the current data sample and past algorithmic randomness, as the proof already assumes.
issues.overall_effect: Under couplings allowed by the written assumptions, the mean direction is biased and the convergence and covariance results can be centered at the wrong point.
issues.title: Sketch–sample independence is used without being imposed
issues.why_classification: Making the proof's standard independent-draw condition an explicit hypothesis repairs the intended method locally, without changing its construction or rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, under Assumptions \ref{ass:2} and \ref{ass:4}, the following \mbox{results}~hold~(recall that $C^\star$ is defined in~\eqref{exp:Cstar}):

issues.failure_explanation: Even after correcting the filtration and independence setup, transferring the contraction bound from B_t to B* requires establishing B_t→B*. Convergence of x_t alone does not establish this under Assumptions 2 and 4: neither controls stochastic Hessians or justifies passing a second derivative through expectation. Smooth sample functions can have Hessians at x* different from the Hessian of their expectation when that interchange fails. Thus parts (c) and (d) use an unestablished Hessian-limit premise.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add Assumption 3 to the lemma and establish B_t→B* using the bounded Hessian martingale differences, continuity, and averaging before passing the projection bound to the limit.
issues.overall_effect: The preparation lemma is unsupported under its own stated hypotheses. Its substantive later applications already impose the missing Hessian assumptions.
issues.title: The limiting sketch-contraction lemma lacks Hessian assumptions
issues.why_classification: This is a local supporting-lemma hypothesis correction; all main applications already include Assumption 3, so their scope and rates need not change.
